svg.title: Figure V2 — Wan2.2 A14B selects experts as the denoising schedule progresses. The stage-transition arrow spans timestep evaluations; it does not chain both experts inside one forward evaluation. Each expert is stored in its respective checkpoint. Both occupy GPU weight memory only if both remain on GPU; only the selected expert runs in a branch evaluation. Official rounded counts are about 27B total and about 14B active, not an inferred per-expert parameter split. Stage widths are schematic and do not encode step counts. Explicit offload changes residency and adds transfers. This is a different model from the dense 5B example. [1P][FACT].
svg.desc: A blue resident-bank outline encloses high-noise and low-noise expert checkpoints. Dashed links connect each checkpoint to its stage. Text labels progress across the denoising schedule and states that two experts do not run within one forward evaluation. A rightward stage arrow joins high-noise to low-noise processing across timesteps. About 14 billion parameters are active per evaluation; about 27 billion are GPU-resident only if both experts remain on GPU. Stage widths do not encode step counts. Offload adds weight transfers.
